dedupe_keys.name: cameo software suite epa and noaa aloha cameo chemicals cameo data manager and marplot for chemical emergency planning

description: A set of free programs that emergency planners and responders use for chemical incidents. The EPA page says the Computer-Aided Management of Emergency Operations (CAMEO) suite has been co-developed by EPA and NOAA since 1988, helps communities plan for and respond to emergencies and meet chemical inventory reporting under EPCRA, runs on Macintosh and Windows with offline use, and has five programs used separately or together: ALOHA, an atmospheric dispersion model that estimates threat zones from toxic gas clouds, fires and explosions; CAMEO Chemicals, a database of response datasheets for thousands of chemicals with a reactivity prediction tool, also as a website and mobile app; CAMEO Data Manager for facility and chemical inventory records; MARPLOT for mapping threat zones against hospitals, schools and other sites; and a fifth tool not read in full. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): EPA web policy: EPA-produced content is in the public domain unless otherwise specified (software licence not stated separately). Coverage is any location, with US regulatory data built in. Caveats: ALOHA is a screening model for short releases. For simulation it links chemical inventories, release modelling and maps of exposed facilities in one workflow. A related catalogue record is ALOHA.
